items.prompt: Explain which rural scheme to fund first in a fictional village. Growers have buyers. An existing usable road causes delays and transport losses; repair would reduce those losses. A seed loan would increase output and can be repaid after harvest, but adds repayment risk. Funds cover only one first. The aim is more dependable net sales.
items.canonical_answer: Road repair can preserve more of the existing harvest and lower delivery losses without adding farmers’ debt. A seed loan can expand saleable output, but repayment remains due if the harvest or prices disappoint. Prioritise repair where current transport losses are large enough to outweigh the extra output from seed. If losses are minor and input shortage is decisive, the loan could offer the better gain. Compare retained sales after costs rather than output alone.

items.prompt: Explain whether a seed loan suits this fictional household. Suitable water, skills and buyers exist. Repayment follows harvest and the expected return exceeds borrowing cost, but a poor season could leave a debt. A smaller self-financed planting has lower expected income and no repayment obligation.
